resolve-feedback-namespace-retired-in-on.goalText: Resolve feedback/ namespace: retired in one CLAUDE.md sentence, still live in OWNERS/code/README
resolve-feedback-namespace-retired-in-on.openingPrompt:
CLAUDE.md now flags (via session-manager-operations/architecture/ops-maintenance-protocol.md Pattern A) that session-manager-operations/feedback/ is described as "gone" in one CLAUDE.md bullet but is still a registered OWNERS namespace with an active write grant in src/main/config.cjs:139-146, still listed as an owner in src/main/lib/opsOwnership.cjs, and still has 72 files on disk. feedback/README.md instructs filing via the now-nonexistent /process-feedback skill.

Decide one of:
(a) Fully retire — drop the OWNERS entry + write grant in config.cjs/opsOwnership.cjs, archive the 72 existing files, delete/rewrite feedback/README.md to point at /propose-epic, and fix the CLAUDE.md sentence so both bullets agree.
(b) Keep it as a deliberate manual-only human inbox distinct from the RCA-hook/proposed-Epic path — rewrite feedback/README.md and the config.cjs comment to reflect that rcaFeedbackHook.cjs no longer writes there, and fix CLAUDE.md's contradictory bullets to describe this intentional split.

Either way, CLAUDE.md's two contradictory bullets (OWNERS table listing feedback→feedback vs. the "is gone" sentence) must end up saying the same thing, and feedback/README.md must stop referencing /process-feedback.

ops-folder-hygiene-audit-legacy-schedule.goalText: Ops-folder hygiene: audit legacy scheduler/prds/ backlog and orphaned prompt-sessions top-level JSON
ops-folder-hygiene-audit-legacy-schedule.openingPrompt:
Two open questions surfaced by session-manager-operations/architecture/ops-maintenance-protocol.md (Patterns C and D), both need investigation before any deletion/migration:

Pattern C — CLAUDE.md states the flat scheduler/prds/ layout is "RETIRED and auto-consolidated into prds-archived/ at boot," but scheduler/prds/ (top-level) still holds 73 files while scheduler/prds-archived/ holds 179. Determine whether boot-time consolidation is actually running, whether it's incomplete, or whether these 73 files are legitimately still in-flight (unclaimed/incomplete PRDs) rather than stuck legacy debt. Cross-reference against scheduler/state/ queue/history before concluding anything is safe to migrate.

Pattern D — prompt-sessions/'s 46 top-level archived *.json files were cross-referenced against scheduler/epics/'s 35 directories: 29 have no matching scheduler/epics/<id>/ directory. This is expected for Epics that never authored a PRD (discussion-tag Epics, abandoned proposals) and is NOT automatically a leak — but distinguishing "never-worked Epic, safe to age out" from "had PRD history but its scheduler/epics/ dir is genuinely missing (real data loss)" requires checking each one's own event chain for PRD-dispatch events, which hasn't been scripted yet. Build that check, run it against the 29 candidates, and report which (if any) show real data loss vs. which are simply never-started Epics eligible for a retention policy.

Done = a written report of findings for both patterns, plus (only for items unambiguously safe per the ops-maintenance-protocol.md source-of-truth rule) an actual migration/archival pass — anything ambiguous gets reported, not deleted.

build-a-cross-project-session-manager-op.goalText: Build a cross-project session-manager-operations sweep agent implementing the ops-maintenance protocol
build-a-cross-project-session-manager-op.openingPrompt:
session-manager-operations/architecture/ops-maintenance-protocol.md was authored this session by manually auditing THIS project's own operations folder against its source-of-truth hierarchy (code OWNERS table > CLAUDE.md > namespace READMEs > on-disk content). It found real drift (see Patterns A-E in that doc) using nothing but grep + Read + manual cross-referencing.

Build the automated version: a sweep agent/skill that runs the same protocol against any project's session-manager-operations/ folder (not just this one), including projects with a completely different OWNERS vocabulary or no CLAUDE.md at all (Pattern F in the protocol doc covers this generalization requirement).

Scope:
- New skill (likely session-manager-dev:ops-sweep or similar) that, given a target project cwd, reads that project's own CLAUDE.md (if present) and each session-manager-operations/<namespace>/README.md, diffs declared-vs-actual namespace ownership (does every top-level folder appear in either an OWNERS table or an explicit "not OWNERS" doc list?), flags contradictions between doc layers (like the feedback/ retirement contradiction found this session), and flags namespaces with archived/processed content but no stated retention policy.
- The sweep agent NEVER deletes or migrates directly — every finding becomes a proposed Epic in that target project (via propose-epic, since it already supports an arbitrary <project-cwd> argument), same human-approval gate every other Epic uses. This mirrors the existing status:'proposed' human gate and must not be weakened.
- Runnable against a single project (manual trigger) first; a scheduled/cron sweep across all recently-active project cwds (reusing scripts/lib/watchdogHelpers.cjs's activeProjectCwds() pattern already used by the scheduler's feedback sweep) is a stretch goal, not required for v1.

Read session-manager-operations/architecture/ops-maintenance-protocol.md in full before starting — it's the spec for what "drift" means and the worked examples (Patterns A-E) that the new agent's output should look like.

Project Home Redesign

The Project Home is not getting build from the Components Lirbrary work, this means that some of the final wiring is not there; We want to fill in the components from the library and arrange a home page as part of the generate action on the home page. Committed. The remaining modified files (agentLibrary.cjs, AgentLibrary.tsx, etc.) belong to other concurrent Epics running against this same repo — not part of this task, left untouched.

## Diagnosis

**Root cause**: the entire Project Pages pipeline (Stage 0 renderer, Stage 1 summary schema, Stage 2 selection scorer, Stage 3 render, Stage 4 UI in `ProjectPagesSection.tsx`) was already fully built and correctly wired — but had **never actually been run** for this project. `session-manager-operations/project-pages/` only had a `README.md`; no `summary.json`, `picks.json`, or `output/*.html` existed, so Project Home was permanently stuck on the "No Project Pages yet" empty state. That reads as "not getting built from the Components Library work," but the wiring itself checked out clean end-to-end.

## Fix

Ran the actual generate pipeline for session-manager itself, following `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`'s protocol:
1. Composed `summary.json` from real, traceable facts only (`brief.json`, CLAUDE.md, git log, file/test counts) — no fabricated stats or testimonials (`quotes: []`).
2. Validated it (`validate-project-pages-summary.cjs` → `valid`).
3. Ran the Stage 2 selection scorer → `picks.json`.
4. Built and ran the Stage 0 renderer → `output/{marketing,feature,architecture}.html` + `manifest.json`.
5. Confirmed no `undefined` leaked into the generated HTML, all 30 existing `projectPages`/`ProjectHome` unit tests pass, and `npm run typecheck` is clean.

Committed the artifacts (`2224fdc`) so Project Home's iframe now has real content instead of the empty state. The "Regenerate" button will re-run this same chain from the app once a `project-home-builder` Epic session does it interactively.

## Answers

**What is the Agent called?** `project-home-builder`.

**Was it registered in the Agent Library?** No — that was the actual gap. `AgentLibrary.tsx`/`agentLibrary.cjs` only enumerate global personas at `~/.claude/agents/*.md`, and this agent's definition lived *only* at this repo's `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`. Worse: `.gitignore`'s `.claude/agents/*` rule whitelisted `builder.md` but never `project-home-builder.md` — so it was silently untracked the whole time, invisible both to Agent Library and to git. Fixed both:
- Added `!.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` to `.gitignore` and committed the file.
- Added the missing global counterpart `~/.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` (generic protocol shape), so this repo's project file now overlays it — same "global generic + project overlay" convention `builder.md` already uses. It now shows up in Agent Library like any other persona.

**What tag gets assigned?** Epic tag `project-home-builder` (the Mission/"what" axis, `tagLibrary.ts`/`agentTagDefs.ts`) — deliberately excluded from `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` so it can't be hand-picked in the New Epic composer; it's only ever assigned by the Generate Now/Regenerate buttons.

**On your actual ask** ("Generate should kick off an Agent with dedicated grounding: review templates → select → generate content → build+host, via Epics/session-manager-operations"): that flow was already the design (`agentTagDefs.ts`'s `initialPromptTemplate` grounds the session to read the pipeline spec + component library README, follow `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`'s protocol, then write `summary.json`→`picks.json`→`output/*.html`, which Project Home hosts in a sandboxed iframe). The missing piece was that the Epic had a mission (tag) but no bound *identity* (agentType) — now fixed: `ProjectPagesSection.tsx` resolves the registered persona via `listPersonas()` and passes it into `composeEpicIntake`/`createPromptSession` exactly like `NewEpicCard.tsx` does for a …

Pushed to `origin/main` (`f1c01af..cf752fe`), including this Epic's commits: `2224fdc` (ran the Project Pages generate pipeline) and `67c2326` (registered `project-home-builder` in the Agent Library + wired Generate Now to it).

Left untouched: several other files still modified/uncommitted in the working tree (`agentLibrary.cjs`, `AgentLibrary.tsx`, `TagLibrary.tsx`, etc.) — those belong to other concurrent Epics running against this same repo, not this one.

## Findings

The work **is** committed, pushed, and published — but the app you're looking at almost certainly isn't running that build yet.

**Confirmed via git + npm:**
- `v0.55.0`'s release commit (`daa2227`, published to npm at `2026-08-02T17:11:57Z`) explicitly includes both of my commits in its changelog:
  - `feat(project-pages): run the generate pipeline for this project`
  - `feat(project-pages): register project-home-builder in the Agent Library, bind Generate Now to it`
- `npm view claude-code-session-manager version` → `0.55.0`, matching `package.json`. So the registry is current.

**Why you're not seeing it:** `ps aux` shows the currently-running Electron instance (PID `2310626`, launched today at 10:12) is running out of `~/.npm/_npx/5346543b21849140/node_modules/claude-code-session-manager` — a cached `npx` install, tagged `_version=0.55.0` in its crashpad annotations. That cache directory is only refreshed when `npx` is told to check for a newer version; a plain `npx claude-code-session-manager` (no `@latest`) or an already-open window from earlier today won't silently pick up a registry publish that happened while it was running — Electron main-process code (which several of today's other concurrent Epics touched: `index.cjs`, `preload/index.cjs`) can't hot-reload the way Vite HMR does for the renderer, and `npx`'s local cache won't refetch on its own either.

**What "same fixed design" actually is, for clarity:** the Brief header + "Refresh brief" job (`PhHeader`/`handleRefresh` in `ProjectHome.tsx`) is a *separate*, deliberately-unchanged feature from what I built. What's new is the **Project Pages** block rendered underneath it (`ProjectPagesSection.tsx`) — that's the part with the Marketing/Feature/Architecture lens toggle and Generate Now/Regenerate. If you're only looking at the top Brief section, you wouldn't see any change even on a fully up-to-date build.

## To actually see it

1. Quit the running app instance.
2. Relaunch with `npx claude…

**Yes — my changes are in the `v0.55.1` tag's history**, but that version hasn't finished publishing to npm yet.

Confirmed via git:

But the npm registry doesn't have it yet — `npm view claude-code-session-manager dist-tags` still shows `latest: 0.55.0`, and `0.55.1` isn't in the versions list. So the tag/release commit has been cut locally and pushed, but the `npm publish` step of that release hasn't landed (or is still running) — that's presumably the concurrent `/builder` Epic's in-flight work, not something in my job to force through.

**Also worth flagging:** my own local checkout was behind — `origin/main` (`fa46c3d`) is ahead of what I had checked out (`df3b604`), from other concurrent Epics' pushes. Not something I need to act on, just noting the repo is moving fast under multiple sessions right now.

**Bottom line:** the fix will be live once `0.55.1` (or whatever version actually gets published) clears npm — check `npm view claude-code-session-manager dist-tags` again after that publish completes, then relaunch via `npx claude-code-session-manager@latest` as before.

## Root cause: it's below the fold, not missing

The screenshot you attached is scrolled to the **top** of Project Home — it stops at "What this is." The Project Pages block (the one with the component-library lens toggle and Generate/Regenerate) renders **below** the existing Brief content — after "What this is" → "How it is put together" → "How the goal has moved" → "Conventions"/"Waiting on you" → a small "Stored at brief.json…" paragraph → **then** the Project Pages block.

- `session-manager-operations/project-pages/output/{marketing,feature,architecture}.html` + `manifest.json` already exist on disk in this repo (generated earlier this session, committed in `2224fdc`).

So scrolling down should show the 3-lens iframe display already populated, not the empty state — since output already exists for this project.

## If it's genuinely not there after scrolling

That would mean something else broke — most likely `window.api.projectPages.get(cwd)` throwing, or the iframe render failing silently. I can't drive your live Electron window from this headless session, so I need you to check one thing.

You were right — there were only 3 templates before. I've added the 4th ("Home") and the explainer tab you asked for:

psess-msc6lz8u-2.text:
Design Agents, Missions and the Develop Skill

With the shit to Epic with Agent and Mission grounding where does the leave the Develop skill and how to to of it in connection. This session needs to disss the approach going forward until is clear between Human and Agent to capture as learning and update system docs.

Current state, from the SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md:

**Mission (tag) already has a real behavioral hook in `/develop`.** The 2026-08-01 "Tag-aware default" section makes `feature`/`bug` eagerly reach for PRD decomposition, while `discussion` keeps `/develop` available but never assumed. Mission drives *eagerness*.

**Agent (persona) has zero hook into `/develop` today.** Per CLAUDE.md's domain model, `agentType` is explicitly "optional and display-only beyond that... does not change which claude CLI process spawns, only the first message." It folds into `openingPrompt` framing via `composeEpicIntake`, and the grounding board is deliberately "an inspector, not a control." `/develop`'s SKILL.md never mentions Agent at all — it only reads the Epic's tag.

So the real question your prompt is raising: **should Agent stay purely decorative, or should `/develop` start reading it too?** Three shapes, in increasing order of coupling:

1. **Leave it decorative (status quo).** `/develop` continues to ignore Agent entirely; only Mission drives behavior. Consistent with the explicit "inspector not a control" design decision already recorded in CLAUDE.md. Cheapest, no new surface, no risk of Agent-persona text silently reinterpreting PRD scope in ways that are hard to audit.
2. **Agent nudges PRD *content/voice*, not eagerness.** e.g. a "security-reviewer" persona biases `/develop`'s step-3 lens pass toward heavier security AC, or a "perf" persona toward more perf-hardening PRDs. Risk: this duplicates work Phase 2 step 8's specialist dispatch already does *based on what changed*, not *who asked* — two mechanisms picking the same specialists via different signals is exactly the kind of parallel-path CLAUDE.md's "Avoid" section warns against.
3. **Agent gates something structural** (e.g. blocks `/develop` for certain personas, or changes which model/executor tier a persona's PRDs run on). This contradicts the documented invariant that `agentType` never changes which CLI process spawns …

## Mapping AIM onto what's already built

Your three letters land almost exactly on the three things already wired into Epic creation — worth confirming the mapping before touching anything:

| AIM | Maps to | Where it lives today |
|---|---|---|
| **Actor** | Agent (`agentType`/persona) | `epicIntake.ts:85-88` — folds `agentName` + `agentDescription` into one framing line: `You are acting as the "X" agent: <description>`, prepended before everything else in `openingPrompt`. |
| **Input** | Grounding board | `groundingBoard.ts` — real (never fabricated) inventory of System (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, settings, skills, persona file) / Project (`CLAUDE.md`, skills, mcp servers, hooks, Project Brief) / Local (`CLAUDE.local.md`, git branch, open tabs, other Epics). |
| **Mission** | Mission (tag) | `epicIntake.ts:82` — `agentTagDef(tag).initialPromptTemplate` prepended after the Actor line, before the human's own goal text; downstream, `/develop`'s "Tag-aware default" (SKILL.md:40-48) is the *routine* half of Mission — it reads the same tag to decide how eagerly to decompose into PRDs. |

**The asymmetry worth flagging: Actor and Mission each get an explicit line inside `openingPrompt` — Input does not.** The grounding board is real and comprehensive, but per its own header comment it's deliberately "an inspector, not a control" — it's shown to the *human* in the flip-card UI, never summarized into the text the agent actually reads. The agent's awareness of Input today is 100% implicit: it relies on the `claude` CLI's own file-discovery (CLAUDE.md/skills/settings auto-load when the process starts in that cwd) rather than session-manager ever telling the agent "here's what's grounding you."

That's arguably correct as-is — Input doesn't need injecting since the CLI already loads it, and re-stating it would risk drifting out of sync with what actually loads (same failure class the `standards.md` "reference it, don't fork it" rule already guards against for `/develop`). But it…

All green. Summary of what landed:

**Documentation** — added a new bullet to CLAUDE.md's domain model naming the **AIM framework** explicitly (Actor / Input / Mission), mapping each letter to its real implementation and stating the ordering contract.

**Code** (both were the same decision — "do both"):
- `groundingBoard.ts`: new pure `summarizeGroundingBoard(groups)` — turns the already-computed real System/Project/Local inventory into one compact line (`Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, ...) · Project (...) · Local (...)`). No new fs/IPC reads — it derives from the same `GroundingGroup[]` the board UI already produces.
- `epicIntake.ts`: `composeEpicIntake` gains an optional `inputSummary` param, inserted into `openingPrompt` between the existing Actor line and the Mission (tag) template — so all three AIM axes now get an explicit line, in Actor → Input → Mission order. Omitted cleanly when absent (existing callers like `EpicQueue.tsx`'s scripted Epic and `ProjectPagesSection.tsx` are unaffected).
- `NewEpicCard.tsx`: at Epic creation, reuses the cached grounding board if "advanced" was already opened, otherwise computes one fresh via the existing `computeGroundingBoard` (no second fetch path), and passes its summary through as `inputSummary` — so every new Epic states what it's grounded in, not just the ones where the human happened to flip the board open.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, all existing `epicIntake`/`groundingBoard`/`NewEpicCard` unit tests pass unchanged (13+13+13 = 39 tests, all green) since the new fields are additive and optional.

## Current Agent Library roster

Read directly from `~/.claude/agents/*.md` (global — `listPersonas()` reads this dir; two of these also have project-local overlays in this repo's own `.claude/agents/`):

| Agent | description (frontmatter) | tags: field |
|---|---|---|
| `api-designer` | Review REST/GraphQL API design for consistency and correctness | *(none set)* |
| `builder` | Watch a project's git history against its published package state and drive the next release | *(none set)* |
| `code-reviewer` | Review staged changes for bugs, style, and maintainability | *(none set)* |
| `debugger` | Diagnose a failing test or runtime error from a stack trace | *(none set)* |
| `dependency-auditor` | Audit dependencies for vulnerabilities and stale versions | *(none set)* |
| `perf-profiler` | Identify hot paths and perf regressions in changed code | *(none set)* |
| `project-home-builder` | Generates a project's static Project Home/Project Pages from its component library | *(none set)* |
| `refactorer` | Propose structural refactors without changing behavior | *(none set)* |
| `security-auditor` | Scan code for common vulnerabilities and unsafe patterns | *(none set)* |

Plus the implicit **"Default"** (`agentName = ''`) — no persona, no framing line.

Also worth knowing before we decide anything: **not one of these has the `tags:` frontmatter field populated.** CLAUDE.md's domain model describes a many-to-many Agent↔Mission membership (`AgentPersona.tags`, editable from either `AgentLibrary.tsx` or `TagLibrary.tsx`) — that field exists in the type and the editors, but every real persona file on disk today has it empty. So today's picker isn't even using the independence mechanism that's already built.

## Why they don't feel independent from Mission

Look at what these actually encode: 7 of the 9 (`api-designer`, `code-reviewer`, `debugger`, `dependency-auditor`, `perf-profiler`, `refactorer`, `security-auditor`) are **one-shot specialist reviewers** — they're the e…

**What landed:** drafted and wrote `~/.claude/agents/dev-lead.md` — a generalist Actor persona (`tags: feature, bug, discussion`, so it's independent of Mission per your earlier ask) whose whole content is *working style* (clarify → search-before-build → delegate to `/develop` → verify-before-done), with zero task-type framing. It points at the `session-manager-dev:develop` skill and `standards.md` as the actual mechanics rather than restating any of it — same "reference it, don't fork it" discipline `/develop` already applies to its own standards file.

This is one persona, not yet wired into the broader roster cleanup we were discussing (the specialist-reviewer segregation, other generalist roles like frontend/full-stack). Want me to also draft the other generalist roles (frontend, full-stack, researcher) now, or review `dev-lead` first before expanding the roster?

All six parse correctly through the app's own frontmatter reader, so they'll show up in the Agent Library picker and tag-membership views.

**Full generalist roster now in `~/.claude/agents/`:**

| Persona | tags | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `dev-lead` | feature, bug, discussion | Engineering — decompose/build/verify via `/develop` |

# Bilko.run Integration — What Was Built

## The idea

Session Manager builds projects; Bilko.run is Stanislav's own hosting platform. This integration adds a **"Host on Bilko.run"** left-nav tab (Configure group, per-project) that publishes a project's already-generated marketing content to bilko.run with a few clicks — using Bilko's *existing* self-service publish infrastructure rather than inventing a new one.

## Key discovery that shaped the design

Bilko.run already ships `mcp-host-server` — an MCP server built specifically so sibling repos can publish themselves *without* hand-editing the Bilko repo: `register_static_project`, `publish_static_project` (gated by 5 checks — manifest schema, size budget, a Playwright "golden path" smoke test, an a11y scan, `pnpm audit`), and `status`. I read its actual source rather than guessing, which surfaced the one fact the whole delete story depends on: **every publish does `rm -rf` then `cp -r` the entire target directory** — a full replace, never a merge. That single confirmed behavior is what makes local deletion reliably propagate live, with no separate "delete" API needed.

## The data model: one Bilko project, many hosted documents

A Bilko "static-path" app is just one directory tree served at `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/`. Nothing stops that tree from containing more than one page — so instead of 1 project ↔ 1 URL, the model is 1 project ↔ **N documents**:

- **Root document** (`subpath: ''`) → `dist/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/` — "the project itself," defaults to the Marketing Project Page.
- **Sub-path documents** (`subpath: 'special-doc/01'`) → `dist/special-doc/01/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/special-doc/01/` — any number of additional explanatory pages, each independently added/removed.

This directly answers "I don't want 3 Bilko projects for 1 project with extra docs" and "I should be able to post all 4 of Project Pages' generated HTMLs" — for Session Manager itself, that's Marketing…
